utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody. Before the witness is being brought in, the Registrar would like to make a correction for the record.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Good morning. I would like to indicate that P1022, marked for identification yesterday, is admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday at the end of the -- the hearing, we had a discussion about the videos, the admissibility of documents and about the question if the witness Janc is the perfect witness to introduce these documents, as Mr. McCloskey indicated yesterday. The Chamber has a different view. I think it must be very clear that it is, firstly, not a question of if there's an objection by the other party, but it's the Chamber who has to decide about admissibility and to protect the rights of the parties. The second question is that we still have no indication that this witness can testify about the content of the videos but only about the chain of custody, how the OTP received these documents, otherwise, the -- the content of the videos should be explained by other witnesses and introduced by other witnesses. And, on the other hand, the question if this witness, Mr. Janc, is the perfect or correct or right witness should have been elaborated at the beginning of his testimony so that the Chamber is in the position to understand the background. It was a quite late stage of the testimony of this witness who was, at the beginning, introduced as a witness about exhumations but not about the videos. But, nevertheless, I just wanted to clarify the situation, why we were not inclined to make decisions about the admissibility of the videos yesterday and why we postponed our decision thereon. I just wanted to make the position of the Chamber clear in this respect. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I think Mr. Janc is principally chain of custody, how we got the videos, so that we can play them. It -- we thought it would be convenient for him to identify a few people. But that's obviously a problem. So we won't do that, and -- but if -- if it's all right with you, we will continue to have him identify how we got things so can you see how we got them and -- and a bit of -- there's some authentication material too that I think you will -- that actually relate to his forensics ability in one of these videos. If we could go on as we did, but I think we will pull the -- his views on who people are and -- but just continue to provide you with the information, where it came from, how we got it, so that you can see that it just didn't come there here haphazardly. Though sometimes they do come in haphazardly but he will explain that as well. If -- if that's all right. And I -- the -- and if you could possibly give us some indication of, for example, the video of -- of Salapura, Mladic, the guy with the white T-shirt, who in your view would be better placed than a knowledgeable investigator, or is it just a matter of we should tell you beforehand which investigator and what he plans to say. Is there someone besides Mr. Janc that you had in mind, or is it a matter of just more -- more foreknowledge as is appropriate in the normal situation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: First of all, it's up to the Prosecution to decide how to introduce a witness and their documents. On the other hand, it is for the preparation of the Defence very important to know in advance, and this is the reason why we have this rule about 65 ter witness summaries, what a witness will testify about. And I think we can proceed on that basis today, but we wanted to clarify our position, why we are not in a position to decide about the admissibility of these documents immediately. So I think if there is no -- nothing else to add and to discuss, we should -- Mr. Vanderpuye was the first.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning to you, good morning, Your Honour. Good morning, everyone. I did want to clarify one thing and that is with respect to Mr. Janc's testimony, the scope of his testimony. We did make the Defence aware that Mr. Janc would be testifying on this subject matter. As I mentioned yesterday, part of the reason why Mr. Janc is testifying on this specific topic at this time, as you recall he is in the middle of cross-examination on a different issue, is a matter of convenience and also a matter of opportunity as well, given the scheduling and the tensions gap in the evidence that's been put before the Trial Chamber. So I just want to make that clear, that the Defence was on notice of the scope of -- of Mr. Janc's testimony with respect to this subject matter. The other thing I wanted to mention was that in respect of Rule 89(C), in terms of the admissibility of evidence, it is incumbent upon the Prosecution to at least demonstrate the prima facie relevance of the material that you're viewing. And to the extent that Mr. Janc may offer evidence that relates to the relevance of the material that you're seeing is -- as distinct from the chain of chain of custody, I would submit that that's an appropriate area for him to testify about, assuming that it's within his knowledge, or within his -- within -- within the -- his experience in order to establish the necessary relevancy for admissibility purposes under Rule 89. I understand that, and I agree with Mr. McCloskey completely, that if the Trial Chamber wants us to refrain from eliciting that material we will do that. But I think -- I think there is some room there for it, because it's incumbent upon us to demonstrate relevancy and probative value for the purposes of admissibility and that may entail identifying an individual in the video who is intimately involved in the subject matter of the case, such as Petar Salapura, such as General Mladic, such as General Gvero. That's the reason why that evidence is appropriate and relevant in the case. But, obviously, we will abide by whatever the Trial Chamber's ruling is with respect to this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We understand very well the difficulties the OTP have to deal with, especially scheduling, filling up the court time. Indeed, this is a big problem. We know that. And we appreciate that normally always a witness is available and we don't lose court time. This is -- I think we have to appreciate that. You know our position about admissibility. I think I -- it's no need to repeat that again. You should proceed with this witness and I think that -- you have shown good reasons why you think these -- the videos have probative value. But I don't want to repeat what I have said at the outset of today's hearing. Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, good morning to everybody. I would just like to raise two matters very briefly. We have been informed by the OTP that this witness will testify about these videos and their authentication. I would like to make the position of the Defence very clear. We have not objected but we haven't consented either. We have left the matter in the hands of the Bench, and we are very satisfied with your decision, Your Honour. That's what I said to Mr. Vanderpuye or Mr. McCloskey, I'm not sure which, and we will refrain from taking a position on this matter. And as for the second thing, yesterday on page 57 of the transcript, line 19, it reads: "[In English] But with respect to Mr. Tieger's objection." [Interpretation] Instead of that, I believe it should read: "[In English] But with respect to Mr. Tolimir's objection."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think we had a -- not Mr. Tieger but Mr. Tolimir. If I recall it correctly, Mr. Tieger was not in court yesterday. We have it on the screen -- on the record now, and the witness should be brought in. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have just an announcement, I guess, a notice, that we have translations uploaded for P584 and P588.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That clarifies the situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And to make it clear, it is now admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Janc. Welcome to the courtroom again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye has some more questions for you. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Mr. Janc.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Sorry I have to remind you that the affirmation to tell the truth you made months ago still applies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, we're going to continue from yesterday. The next video is a video that is not dated, which we believe is from July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: For the record, it is 65 ter 2436.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you tell us, are you familiar with this video and the circumstances under which the Office of the Prosecutor came into possession of it.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As for the other videos I'm also very well aware of this video, and it is so-called Skorpion video of the killing of six Muslim men in the area of Trnovo in Bosnia-Herzegovina, which is area south of Sarajevo. And the OTP obtained this video on 8th of September, 2004, in Sarajevo from a confidential source. The video itself, it shows six Muslim men which are transported to a certain location by the members of the Skorpion unit and are subsequently killed, executed nearby.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Before we play it, could you just tell us roughly how far Trnovo is from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Trnovo is south of Sarajevo, the area of, I would say, around 50 kilometres from Sarajevo and from Sarajevo to Srebrenica there is about 150 kilometres in addition. So in total I would say, that's my rough estimation of around 200 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And if you're able to, can you tell us a little bit about the Skorpions unit?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel please speak into the microphone for the sake of interpreters. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you tell us a little bit about the Skorpion unit.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Skorpion unit was initially -- was actually established in 1993. Before that, that was a group of individuals who were deployed when the war broke out in Croatia in 1991 by the Krajina oil company in Croatia and they were guarding their facilities there. In 1993, they became a Skorpion unit, and as such, part of the then-army of the Serbian Krajina in Croatia. The unit was disbanded in 1996, in May of 1996, and during this time, they were a kind of a special unit of the army of the Serbian Krajina in Croatia. During this time, they were deployed to Bosnia on three occasions also. First time in 1994 into Bihac area. Then in April of 1995 in Velika Kladusa, also in BiH. And then for the last time, in Trnovo area, in June of 1995. At that time, they were deployed as a members of the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Serbia. Over all these years, the Skorpion unit has a close relations with the State Security of the Republic of Serbia. And in June of 1995, the government of the Republika Srpska, Bosnia and Herzegovina, requested support from the Ministry of Interior from Republic of Serbia, and Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Serbia sent several units, one of those being this Skorpion unit, to the Trnovo battle-field.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'd like to show you 65 ter 5337.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May there be peace in this house for all those present and may God's will be done in these proceedings, and may the outcome be as God wishes and not as I wish. I'm a bit late with my objection because we have moved on to another topic. But I believe the witness has not seen these Skorpions and he is also speaking about persons from the MUP of Serbia whom he hasn't seen either. And this does not correspond to what is captured on the video recording. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The Chamber doesn't know anything about the video yet. We will see that. And, of course, what we have heard from the witness was second-hand knowledge. He was not present at that time. He was not part of the Skorpions and had no direct contact. But this is, I think, obvious, that this is the knowledge he was able to gain during his investigation, and only in this respect, the Chamber will receive this information by the witness. Carry on please, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, can you see the document that's in e-court now?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is this a document that you reviewed in the context of -- of your statements concerning the Skorpions unit?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I did review this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can you tell us what about this document in particular relates to what you've just said about the Skorpion unit?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a report from Ljubisa Borovcanin who was deputy commander of the special police forces of the Ministry of Interior of Republika Srpska at that time, and he is reporting from the forward command post in Trnovo to his -- to several units. You can see addresses there. And in first paragraph of this report, he is talking -- talking about the unit, the units which were active in this Trnovo battle-field, and he lists several names of those units, which are Kajman detachment. I'm reading from the third line of the first paragraph now. Then Plavi. And Skorpion. And then we have in brackets (Serbian MUP). And as I just testified just before, so those three units represented the Serbian MUP at that time. And what is meant by Serbian MUP are the -- are those who represented the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Serbia. Later on, down, we can also see that he is reporting, so several paragraph where it says: "In yesterday's clashes four members of the SBP," which are members of his units, "and three members of the Serbian MUP were lightly wounded." So he is reporting also about the casualties of this unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Are you aware of any situations or circumstances in which the Serbian MUP worked together with Mr. Borovcanin's units and with the units of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were deployed -- actually, there was an order on 10 of July of 1995 from then-deputy minister of interior, Tomo Kovac, deploying these units to Srebrenica to help with the operation on Srebrenica enclave.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you for that. I have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could we please see the second page of the English to have a full picture of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. I think I'd like to play the videotape at this point. So if we could. In a moment I'll give you the reference. It's 65 ter 2436. And we can watch it straight through.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, you've had an opportunity to see the sequence in this video-tape. It's part of the video. Can you describe a little bit for us what precedes this clip that we've just seen, since this isn't the entirety of the video sequence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before you answer, Mr. Janc, I note that there was no French translation on the French channel today. Yesterday we received French translation of the spoken words in B/C/S. Today, not. I don't know the reason for that, but I wanted to put it on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I'm afraid I don't know the reason for it either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, you may proceed and we will receive the -- the answer of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think I was asking if could you describe, briefly and generally, the sequence of events that precedes the clip that we've seen.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's only part of the video, an excerpt from the video we received from this confidential source. It's quite a long video, actually, which starts with the priest again blessing these Skorpion units before they go to the battle-field in Trnovo. And I -- based on the statements from -- from the members of this unit, this is happening in Croatia at their base. And then we have several footages already from Bosnia-Herzegovina when the Skorpion unit arrives in the area. We have footages from Jahorina training centre and later on from the woods when they are preparing for the battle. And then this video-clip, this portion of -- of the video starts.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm going ask you a little bit about the chain of custody with respect to this video. Now you mentioned that you reviewed some documentation concerning the source of this video. Can you tell us what that was.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the main source was, of course, the declaration of the investigator Tore Soldal from 2005 because he was the investigator from the OTP who received, obtained this tape from the confidential source. And in this declaration we have the detailed specific of events which happened and clarification how the OTP obtained this videotape. And, of course, I have reviewed the statements of this confidential source.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Could I have 6574 in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Judge Nyambe has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: I have a question for Mr. Vanderpuye. Is the confidential source on your list of witnesses to be called, the confidential source of this video?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The confidential source of the video is not on the list of witnesses to be called. However, the videographer, the person who took the video, as I understand it, is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We have 6574 in e-court yet? We do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: There must be a reason for confidentiality of this source. Is it because it is a source pursuant to Rule 70 or could it be explained further in the courtroom in private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We can explain it a little bit further in private session. So if we can go into private session, I think I can explain it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In terms of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: One moment please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Carry on, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we go to paragraph 11 - that's on page 3 of this document - you will see in paragraph 11, there's a reference to -- well, it reads: "In early December 2004, other investigators took statements from relatives of two of the victims whose bodies had been exhumed from the site in Trnovo." Do you see that in the document, Mr. Janc?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did have you an opportunity to review any statements of relatives of victims who were exhumed from the site in Trnovo?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did review four of them. Those two which are mentioned here and an additional two which were taken from them earlier on in 2005.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And is the date of the statements that you reviewed -- the date indicated in the statements that you reviewed, is that consistent with the information that's recorded in this declaration?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. It was in December of 2004.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this time I would offer this declaration into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Surprisingly, we have now a B/C/S translation of this page. I would like to know if there are -- the whole document has a translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It does.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. This will be marked for identification and we will decide later, if it will be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 6574 will be Exhibit P1023, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I see that we've got about two or three minutes before the break, and this might be a good opportunity to pause.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Indeed. Mr. Gajic, I see you're on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have a question which I would like to put to the Prosecutor, actually. I think it's about a document -- about document 06573, that's the 65 ter number. The English language version is redacted. Much information is redacted. However, the -- what I can see in Serbian in e-court is not redacted. Perhaps the link between the two documents is wrong or possibly the original English document is missing, so I kindly ask for this to be clarified.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I appreciate the observation. I think that's something that we've got to look into, obviously, given the representations that I've made about the confidentiality of the material. So I will look into that and I will get back to you and the Trial Chamber about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We must have our first break now, and we will resume at 11.00. We adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Our apologies for the delay. We considered the situation during the break, and we want to make clear for the parties the position of the Chamber. We will marked for identification the video we have just seen before the break. The reason to -- only to mark it and not to admit it into evidence now is that Mr. Janc is able to identify the ERN number, to identify that this is in the custody of the OTP, that this was obtained from a source which is protected, pursuant to Rule 70 of our Rules; but, of course, he is not the right witness to identify what is depicted in the video: When did this shooting take place, where did that take place, what is the background and so on. I don't want to go into details. We are convinced that this video has a probative value but we need more information, and we realised that on the list to be called of the Prosecution there is Slobodan Stojkovic, and he will be in the position to explain what depicted in the video, when was the video shot, and so on. And, therefore, we would like to invite the Prosecution to -- to give us by this witness or in another way, more information about the -- what we have seen in the video, when it -- when this happened, and where this killing took place. This is, of course, very important for the whole case. Therefore, this video will be marked for identification. One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 2436 will be Exhibit P1024, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We will also mark for identification the declaration of the interpreter -- of the investigator of the OTP. I don't recall his name at the moment. It is on the screen now. That will be marked for identification as well because Mr. Janc told us that he saw it the first time before -- or during his preparation of his testimony for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I did intend to lead further evidence concerning the -- the content of the video, that is, the location, and other, I think, important information concerning its authenticity and reliability, and certainly its relationship to the salient issues in this case, including the information concerning the victims and the exhumation of the site which I think are clearly relevant and probative of matters under the indictment. And I think Mr. Janc is particularly acquainted with this information and -- and this would be helpful to the Trial Chamber, certainly in consideration of this video. So that was my plan and then I plan to proceed also with two other videos, which I hope to get through as well. I'm reminded by Ms. Stewart that I have not tendered 65 ter 5537. This was a document that I did actually show Mr. Janc and this is the document, I think it's dated 1st July, 1995, and referring to the Skorpion unit and we had it up on the screen in the record. So I would tender this document at this time as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can we have that back on the screen, please. I think it was the order of Mr. Ljubisa Borovcanin; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It is a report. I just want to make sure I have the number right, though. Yes, it's 5 -- I'm sorry, it is 5337.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think this is correct. I would like to ask Mr. Janc from whom did the OTP obtain this document? Can you tell us a little bit about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, from the top of my head, I would not be able to say right now. Based on the ERN number, I think it's part of the Republika Srpska MUP collection, but I would rather check -- check it further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: When have -- do you recall when you have seen this document first?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I've seen this document, I think, around three times so far, and for first, I would say, few years ago already. But I cannot say exactly when. And also when I have been preparing for this testimony I reviewed it once more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This document will be marked for identification. Because of the content of the testimony of Mr. Janc, we're just not precisely clear about the chain of custody of this document and from where it was obtained, and -- in relation to the content of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 5337 would be Exhibit P1025, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, in respect of your review of this video that we've just seen concerning the events in Trnovo and the execution, the executions that we've seen, were you able to ascertain additional information concerning the location at which this -- these events occurred?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was able to ascertain this additional information regarding the location.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what is the nature of the information that you ascertained?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally never was at this particular location, but several other members of the OTP, including Investigator Soldal, were there at that location in 2005. And in September of 2005, there was also an OTP photo-visual technician, Mr. Zoran Lesic, who attended the site, and I talked to him during the course of preparation for my testimony, and, of course, I've read his statement he has given to Mr. Tore Soldal. In relation to the presentation of the site and corroboration with the videos we have just -- video we have just seen, I talked to him and, yeah, I got aware of -- of the location and during the presentation will go over what he made, I think, in 2005.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'd like to have 65 ter 6576 shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you recognise what we have here in e-court now, Mr. Janc?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the beginning of the presentation and it is the aerial image of the area where the shooting took place, the shooting from the video we have just seen, and if you click on -- on this photo for first time ...

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Tell us what we see here.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the left-hand side, we can see we have an arrow which says "arrival site." This is the place when we can see the truck has parked, and then the Muslim men are taken off the truck and lie down on -- on the ground. This is the place, the location from that video. On the right-hand side of this photo, we see several buildings there, and the arrows which -- the arrow which depicts the execution site. So this is the location where we can see these men -- these four of those Muslim men being executed. To the right-hand side of this arrow, we can see a white renovated building, and inside this building, the last two of those six Muslim men from the video were executed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me ask you before we go on, did you put these arrows in this particular exhibit?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. Everything what we can see on this presentation was made by Zoran Lesic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did you compare what is indicated in this exhibit to what you observed in the video itself?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did compare. I did review. This presentation did compare to all the information we have here in relation to this execution. And I have to also add that this presentation is compilation of the photographs which were taken during Zoran's site visit in September of 2005, and then we see some footages from -- some stills from the actual execution video we have just seen, and also there will be one or two photos at the end showing -- which were taken from the video of the exhumation of those six individuals which was conducted by the BiH authorities in April of 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And with respect to the markings that we see here, arrival site and execution site, on this -- in this frame of the exhibit, does that conform accurately to what you personally observed in the video?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that. And when we will be going to these specific locations, we'll see -- because it's a 360-degrees presentation we will see the actual footages from the site, and then in -- we'll compare those to the stills from the -- from the execution video.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Let's move ahead then.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we go to the site -- where it says "arrival sites," to that part of the video, and we click on it. Okay. Now we have here the actual bridge you can see, and if we turn around, so this is 360 degrees so this is actually how it looks like at the spot. Okay. So let's go around. Okay. Stop. So here is a bridge and there is a river or stream which you can also hear on the video itself. So if you -- if you listen carefully you would see in the background a stream of water. So that's because they are very close to this water. So, and the actual truck stops in front of this bridge. And if we go around a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: To the right or --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the right, please, yes. So go to the right. Okay, stop it here. So this is the location on the right-hand side where you can see the Muslim men lying on the ground. And if we can click in the middle of the picture here, yes. So now this is taken from the actual video we have just seen. And if you click it again. So this is another picture from this same video. And we can click it once more. And now can you see the actual road, the -- the photo which was taken in 2004. And if we go around, move around for 180 degrees, so -- okay. Stop here. So the bridge and behind the bridge you can see a little hill which is quite a significant one, and if we click in the middle or on that hill, yes, this one, you can see the footage, the still from that video and you can see in -- behind this same hill when these individuals, Muslim men, are walking towards the execution site. And we can click it again. And this is the portion of the video where the other members of the Skorpion unit are coming from that direction. And just below that, there is a -- there is a portion of the bridge which was, at that time, I think, made -- it was a wooden bridge at that time. So yeah, this is the area from the arrival site and we can see them walking up there. And then if can you go back to the main -- main aerial, if you click it up there, yes. Okay. So now we can see that they are walking up from the arrival site on this road and they turn left to the execution -- to the field where they were later on executed, just on the opposite side of the house which we can see underneath the -- this picture. So, and, yeah, I would just like to emphasise also, I also -- I already talked about the renovated house in which the last two men were executed, just a little bit down and right this -- this white house, you can see the foundation of -- of the house. And at that time during the execution there was still a house, but during our site visit it's not there anymore but foundations are still there. And to the far right of the picture, you can see another house which is also -- which can also be seen on the video on the execution video, and we have some stills, additional exhibits prepared later on where we will see both of those houses. Actually, all those three. And now we can move to the actual execution site, if you click it there, on that picture. Okay. Now this is the place where first four men were executed and behind you see this white renovated house now where the last two men were executed. So we can move around a little bit, 360 degrees, so that we can see the area around.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Was there anything particularly distinctive about this area which allowed you to compare it to the footage in the video, in order to determine if it is the correct location or the location depicted in the video?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the video, you can see, for example, those two trees which they have a white colour. I don't know what the word in English is, but those two white trees you can -- I'm not sure if it's those particular ones but such trees you can see also on the video itself. So that's -- that's one indication.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And is there anything distinctive about the building itself?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We'll go to the building, to the building right now. But the building is, as it was renovated, still in a same shape as it was in 1995, but it is just renovated at the time when we -- we were there, the OTP was there. So, and now we can perhaps click on this building. It should be a little bit right. Right to it. More. More -- more right. Here. Okay. Now we are in front of the building. And if we can move a little bit left to it. Or we -- we made a circle around, 360-degree circle first to see the area. Stop it -- just a little bit. Okay. Stop it here first. So here on the left -- right-hand side we can see the foundation of this building which was there before. It's in 1995 but during our site visit, it's not -- it is only the foundation. And on the left-hand side, you see another building which -- which is depicted on the video on the execution itself also.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is that what appears to be in the centre of the -- of the screen here, at this --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And we can click on it. I think we'll have a link to ... no. It's the other side. No, no, no. Go -- go back to execution and go back to that point on -- here. Okay. Now, can we move left a little bit. Okay. Now are in front of the house where those last two individuals were executed. On the left-hand side, you can see the doors. And inside this room they were executed. And on the right-hand side you also have additional doors, and in the middle there is a window. And if you can click on the right-hand side on the green doors now. So this is the -- the video still from the execution and we can see the -- actually there are no doors but the -- and no window but this is exactly the same door and the shape of the door and the same door from that building. Can you click it one more.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You're referring to the frame, the empty frames here that we see?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right, to the empty frames on this -- on this still.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you click it once more. And now we have the video still from the video of the exhumation conducted in 1999. So and we can see here the actual room on the left-hand side where the last two individuals were killed. And, yeah, the same -- the same shape of the building and this is actually taken from the -- from the exhumation video.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Who carried out the exhumation, if you know?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The exhumation was carried out by the BiH authorities, Federal Commission on Missing Person.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Have you reviewed documentation in relation to the exhumation?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. In relation to my exhumation report which I testified about, I have reviewed this stuff, these documents, and I also included -- included them into my report. And this particular site is referred in my report in section of other graves as Godinjske Bare site.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And I just wanted to ask, the position of the door frame, window-frame on the first floor and what appears to be a larger frame on the right of the photograph and the window-frame in the middle on the second floor of this building, are they consistent with the position or relative position of these -- of these openings in the renovated building that we saw before?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They are consistent. They are the same -- the same -- the same position, yes. We can click it, on it again. So ... you can see here that it is the same position still of these frames but now they're doors. If we can move to the left a little bit. Yes, thank you. And now we can click it on those -- those doors. Yes, these ones, on the left-hand side. So this the actual still from the video itself, so the killing of last two Muslim men. And we can see the door and these are the same door [sic] as we have seen on the -- the -- the photo before. And we can click it perhaps once more on this one. So it's a close-up of the individual who is shot. And once more. So, and this is the -- the still taken from the exhumation video so that's how this -- the remains of these individuals were found, so it was -- this is the footage from 1999. Once more, if we click it. So that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. I wanted to ask --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think before you continue, there are several questions by all the three Judges, and Mr. Tolimir wanted to raise something. May I start, who did this compilation we have seen here now, parts of photo, parts of different videos? Who made this compilation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This was made by the OTP photo-visual technician, Mr. Zoran Lesic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And what was your involvement in the preparation of this compilation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When this compilation was prepared, that was in 2005, I was not even the member of the Tribunal yet. So my involvement was just to contact him, to ask him -- to get, if he can provide me with this presentation, and he gave me a tour, like I gave you today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Is Mr. Zoran Lesic still in -- member of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, he is still the member of the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. You told us about exhumation in 1999, and you mentioned a video. We have seen a still of it. Can you tell us something, how the OTP obtained this video?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The OTP requested this video and also along with other exhumation records from the BiH Federal Commission on Missing Persons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You said that the photos we have seen in this compilation were taken in 2004. Who has taken these photos?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, the photos from the site visit, the one is just in front of us, were taken in September of 2004 by Zoran Lesic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Except Mr. Lesic, who took part in this site visit? If you know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not from the top of my head. But there is his statement talking about that so I would need to consult that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And you personally have never been at this site?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: If I have understood you correctly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, you understood me correctly. No, I was never there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Judge Mindua has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have a question that was touched upon by the Presiding Judge. I would like to know, Witness, you said that the renovated house as we see it now, the renovated house dates back to 2004, and exhumations took place in 1999, including the stills that we saw of the last two men that were killed inside the house. Do you know who took those pictures in 1999?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, there is actually a video which was made during the exhumation by the BiH authorities, BiH Federal Commission on Missing Persons, during the exhumation. And we obtained this video, the OTP I mean, and we have taken stills from that video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. This is what I thought I had gathered from what you said, given that the facts have happened or should have happened in 1995. So the OTP states that from 1995 to 1999, this house would not have been tampered with.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, based on the -- on the information we have received, yes, that's the case. Because at that time most probably some attorney came back to this location, and they discovered these mortal remains of the individuals and then that's why this exhumation was conducted. That's my understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Judge Nyambe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Could we go back to the very first still that was shown, showing the execution site and the - right - arrival site. Can you tell the distance from the arrival site to the execution site?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not exact one but I can say a few hundred metres, based on the map I think which we can also see from the bottom of this page. Yes. I think it is 200 metres only.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Okay. Can we go back to it again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And we can see the actual -- if the bridge coordinates at the top in the red square and the house coordinates, and one can easily measure how far away these sites are. So but -- I cannot say from -- just based on this information. I would need some software to do this measuring.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Can we go back to the still again. Are you able to say whether the houses between the two arrows existed at the time of the execution?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I'm not able to say -- to say that. So I would speculate, if can I confirm. But most probably that one, first one, or the second one, from the arrow execution site on the left-hand side site which is still destroyed, this must have existed at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: What was this site? Was it ordinary residential area or an army barracks or something? What was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is the place called Godinjske Bare and it is close to Trnovo, according to the statements I read. 2 to 3 kilometres away from the base where the Skorpion unit has billeted at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: In relation to the summary of your evidence, you are referred to as somebody who is going to give updates on results of exhumations and collection of human remains found on the surface. Were you personally involved in any of these two activities, exhumations and collection of remains from the surface?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, for most of -- yeah, for most of them, I was not present, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I wanted a clarification about whether this gentleman, Mr. Zoran Lesic, who reconstructed the site, had previously seen the footage of the event, and I wanted to ask whether the accused was present when this was done in 1995, but you have already said that he wasn't. So I'm left with the first question only. Did Zoran Lesic see the reconstruction or, rather, make the reconstruction of the site after having seen the recording of the event. And the second question refers to page 37, line 18, where the witness said that the exhumation was in 1999. Whereas, on page 33, line 9, he said that the exhumation was in 2004. So I'm -- I -- I don't know now when it actually was. Could we compare pages -- page 33, line 9, and page 37, line 18. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I see on page 37, line 21, 20 to 21: "And now we have the video still from the video of the exhumation conducted in 1999." This is the reference to the year 1999. And that is what I understood from the witness about the time that the exhumation was conducted. Is that correct, Mr. Janc?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that's correct. The exhumation was conducted in April of 1999.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, does that clarify the situation?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President, but it doesn't. Because in the document that we saw, P1023, in paragraph 11, it reads that in early December 2004, an exhumation was conducted at the site in Trnovo. Now how can both sets of corpses be exhumed -- or, rather, the same sets of corpses be exhumed at two different locations?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In my understanding, this is a typical question to put to a witness during cross-examination. But perhaps you can, Mr. Vanderpuye, pick that question up and continue with Mr. Janc's examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. As you may recall, Mr. Janc has testified about this particular exhumation site and it's contained in his report which was admitted before this Trial Chamber on -- as P16 -- 170 and Annex D of that report which was P167.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, could you perhaps elaborate on your familiarity and information concerning the exhumation which was conducted at the site that you have identified as Godinjske Bare?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. And the video from the exhumation part of which -- or stills of which we have seen during the presentation was conducted in 1999 and that was the main exhumation conducted in that area. But since the -- the mortal remains, the bones, were scattered around the area, I know that there were additional not exhumations but just picking of these additional bones in later time. And you might be correct, Mr. -- General, when saying that there was additional in 2004, and I agree with you that there were at least two visits of the BiH members of the -- for missing persons at that location, but the main exhumation was conducted in 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Could we just have 65 ter 6574 in e-court for a moment. It's P1023. We'll refer to paragraph 11, which is what I think Mr. Tolimir is referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, on page 44, line 10, you are recorded as having said the document is P16170. This can't be correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Indeed, it's not. The document is P170, that's the report. And P167, is the Annex D to the report, both of which are admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And with respect to -- I'd like to have -- I'm sorry, P1023, paragraph 11, please, shown to the witness. It's on page -- page 3 I think in both documents -- both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now General Tolimir referred to paragraph 11 as indicating that an exhumation was conducted in 2004 in this paragraph. The paragraph itself reads that: "In early December 2004, other investigators took statements from relatives of two of the victims whose bodies had been exhumed from the site in Trnovo." 2004, therefore, refers to statements. And it continues: "That on 1 February 2005, the Bosnian government provided with us a letter detailing the exhumation of the victims." Having looked at that, Mr. Janc, can you state with any certainty whether or not General Tolimir is correct that there were exhumations that were conducted in 2004?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Regardless of this information what's written here, I can state with my testimony that there were at least two exhumations there. The one being the main one in 1999, and later on, they picked up additional bones which were found in vicinity of these houses. For sure, they were not -- there was not only one. I -- I do remember reading several different records about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in preparing your report that I referred to just a moment ago, P170, reviewing the information concerning Godinjske Bare, were you able to determine if the location where the exhumations were conducted correspond to the locations that are indicated in the videotape and in the exhibit we just looked at?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it correspond. And Mr. Amir Masovic, who was at the time the head of the Federal Commission on Missing Persons, attended the site together with the OTP investigators in order to show them the exact place where these exhumation took place. And just, I have to also reply to -- to the question of General Tolimir, when he asked about the knowledge of Mr. Lesic before went to a site visit. Yes, I am sure he was aware of this footage and he reviewed this information before he went on a mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Based on your review of the exhumation materials for your report, can you confirm that the locations that are indicated in the exhibit that contains the photographs taken by Mr. Lesic accurately reflect the location where the exhumations occurred and where the killings occurred as depicted in the video?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you do that independently of your -- your conversation with Mr. Lesic regarding this particular exhibit?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's possible, because every exhumation record includes the exact coordinates where this exhumation take place and based on these coordinates, you can pin-point the exact location, and that's how it's possible to be done. And I would -- it is easy to go, then, to that location and to check everything what was done by Mr. Lesic, take a few photographs and make a comparison of the site with the actual exhumation and execution video.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And are the exact -- is the exact location of the exhumations that were carried out in Godinjske Bare contained in your report or referred to in documents that are mentioned in your report?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Godinjske Bare exhumation site is part of my report. It is under section of other graves and the -- I also listed the documents regarding the exhumation of this location. In addition, in the confidential part D of my report, you will find the name of the identified individual -- individuals through DNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in terms of the exhumation material that you examined, can you tell us how these remains were recovered? Were they recovered from the surface or were they recovered -- were they dug out from under the ground?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were most -- most of them on -- on a surface. We can see the footage from inside the house as they were collected from inside the house. But some of them were over the time, because several years elapsed before -- in between, and they were covered with a few centimetres of the soil. And what is very important here is that they were -- bones were scattered around the area and it was -- I can confirm, yes, they were collected from this site.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'd like to offer 6576 into evidence at this time, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Once again, what is this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: This document is the presentation that we just showed, the one with the arrows and the locations and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, the compilation of stills and videos.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, the Chamber will decide on that later. You should proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I'd like to --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You've indicated, Mr. Janc, that the victims that are depicted or shown, I should say, in this video that we've seen, have been identified. Can you tell us what the source of your information is, what is the basis of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were all identified through DNA process by the ICMP, International Commission on Missing Persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'd like to show you, if I may, 65 ter 2435A. Do you recognise what is depicted here, Mr. Janc?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the video -- the still from the same video, from this execution video.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And if we can zoom out just a little bit so we can see the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you see the name here, Safet Fejzic? Mr. Janc, were you able to confirm the identity of this individual; and if you were, can you tell us on what basis?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Apart from the DNA identifications, four of these individuals have also been identified by the -- their relatives. And four of these relatives the OTP interviewed in 2004 and 2005, and one of those being this individual who was identified by his sister.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we can go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you tell us about this individual? Were you able to identify -- were you able to identify this person, indicated here as Juso Delic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This individual was identified through DNA only. We don't have the actual statement of the relatives.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we can go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You see here two individuals, Sidik Salkic and Azmir Alispahic. Were you able to confirm their identity; and, if so, on what basis?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were also both identified by -- identified by the relatives. Sidik Salkic by his son; and Azmir Alispahic by his brother-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And if we can go to -- I think it should be the last page of this exhibit, ending 890.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Here we see an individual identified as Smajil Ibrahimovic. Were you able to confirm his identity; and if so, on what basis?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm. He was identified by his wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, if we can just go one page back, ERN ending 889. We have here a list of six individuals. Number 1 is indicated as Safet Fejzic; number 2 is Dino Salihovic; 3, Juso Delic; 4, Azmir Alispahic; 5, Sidik Salkic; and 6, Smajil Ibrahimovic, who we just saw. With respect to Dino Salihovic, can you confirm his identity and on what basis, if you can?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the individuals under number 1, 4, 5, and 6, they were all identified through their relatives. Individuals under 2 and 3, these are the two you are asking me right now, were identified through DNA. And I was able to conclude who is who based on their date of birth. We can see that the individual under number 3 is older than the individual under number 2. And one was born, based on their data we have in our records, in -- I think in 1970, and the other one, 1979 or 1978. So the individual under number 2 was 16 or 17 years old only at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now with respect to all of these individuals were you able to ascertain whether or not they are in any way connected to the events in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can confirm they are all on the lists of the individuals missing from Srebrenica, and they were reported as missing in 1995, after the fall of Srebrenica. Not only that. Also, from the statements of their relatives which recognised them from this video, it can be concluded that they all departed Srebrenica after the fall together with the column. The individual under number 4, which was identified by his brother-in-law, he departed actually together with him. They were together, part of the column heading towards Tuzla. And that at one point in time when there was heavy shelling, they -- they lost each other and this brother-in-law has never seen him again. So they are all the victims from -- or actually, the individuals which are on Srebrenica missing list.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And the individual identified as Safet Fejzic, number 1 here, you indicated he was identified by his sister?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, by his sister.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did you review her statement?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I also reviewed her statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And based upon your review of that statement, can you say whether or not her statement connects him to the events in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, also her statement connects him to the events in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: For the record, and for Your Honours' benefit -- if we can just go into private session for a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before you move to another document I would like to put one question to the witness. You said some of these individuals were identified by their relatives. Was there, in addition to that, a DNA analysis?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I can confirm for all of -- for all of them, for all six of these individuals, there are DNA confirmations of their identifications.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, at the beginning of your testimony before the summer recess, you -- you were shown lists of DNA analysis and the outcome of such an investigation, and you explained a lot on that. Do you remember if these six individuals were contained in this -- these lists we have seen earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, these six individuals are included into these lists and into my report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I would like to tender 65 ter 2435A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The document will be received as an exhibit, the set of photographs with the names we have seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I just wanted to point out -- oh, I'm sorry, I'll wait.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P1026.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Now carry on, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I just wanted to point out for the Court's benefit that with respect to the DNA evidence in this case, we do expect, and we have the director of forensic science from the ICMP will who come and testify about the DNA process or DNA identification process. In addition to that, you have already Mr. Janc's report concerning this particular exhumation site along with the underlying exhumation and reports and data that support it, and they are referred to in the report itself, and I believe most of them are actually in evidence alongside the report. What I wanted to show the witness is 65 ter 6575.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, are you able to tell us what's on the screen right now? We'll zoom in a little bit in just a moment so that you can see it more clearly.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. This is an exhibit regarding the comparison of the two videos, the site comparison. On the left-hand side, we have the photographs from the execution video we have seen today. And on the right-hand side, we have the photographs from the exhumation video conducted in 1999. And then inside each and every single picture we have red circles which depict the same features on both videos.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And again, I can tell that I haven't produced this exhibit. The only thing which is mine is the heading line which says "From the execution video" and "From the exhumation video." The rest was done by the Case Manager for the then-Milosevic trial, Iain Reid.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. If we could just go and blow up the first row of pictures, just the first row. Make it a little bit bigger, please. Keep going. I think that's all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What we have are two circles in the photograph on the left, and two circles in the photograph on the right. And can you tell us what they represent? What do they show?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, they are showing the -- the same features on both -- on both videos, on both stills. On the left-hand side from execution video and on the right-hand side from the exhumation. So the doors, and the -- the window from the same building.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And are these consistent with the building that we see in the compilation exhibit that we looked at before, the renovated building, that is, the position or relative location of the doors and windows?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the same building.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And is this consistent with your own independent observation in comparing these -- these two video footages?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we can go to the next -- next row down, please. That's row number 2. That's pretty good.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you tell us what we see here? What is being compared?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, from the right-hand side, we have two circles depicting the same door and video -- and window, sorry. On the left-hand side, there is a big red circle around the main doors from the room where the last two Muslim men were executed. And there is then a little red circle which -- which shows the damage on the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. So we're going from left to right. The next circle in the photograph on the left is around what appears to be a window and somebody's head is in that circle. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean on the -- the man in green?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, the photograph on the left.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there are -- these two members -- this is the member of the Skorpion unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And does that circle -- how does that circle relate to the photograph on the right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's -- it depicts the window, the same -- the same window.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And then the last circle in the photograph on the left, can you tell us what that corresponds to in the photograph on the right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are the -- the -- the big doors, I think going to garage from the right-hand side of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Let's go down to the next row, please, row number 3. Can you tell us what's depicted here?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, can you see the -- the features of the -- of the houses behind -- behind this one where those two last men were executed. So on the left-hand side we have a circle about the house which was still there in 2004, and I emphasised that when we have been watching the presentation that that house is still there. But that, on the right-hand side, we have, I think, the circle around this part of the building, the pole, I think, which was there in 1995 and still in 1999 during the exhumation but not anymore in 2004. We have seen there are only foundations of this house.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, photograph on the left, the one with the -- the first circle, that is, from the left side, what circle appears to be quite blurry. Is there any distinctive in that photograph that allows you to make a comparison with the photograph on the right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can see from the left-hand side, we can see the roof of the house in white, so -- and also part of the roof is damaged, so we can see this clearly on both pictures.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let's go to the next row, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you tell us what we see in this row, 4?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, it's basically the same as before. Part of the house, destroyed house, and this -- this pole -- of the second house.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's the same roof and post that are depicted in row 3?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that's -- that's the same house. Both are the same houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let's go down to the last one.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can you tell us what we see here?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is a small red circle around the hook of the doors of the room where the last two men were executed. And down there, you can see even the doors are the same, and we can even see that the -- the hook is damaged. And on the biggest circle, red circle, it depicts this part of the doors which are the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you for that, Mr. Janc.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would like to tender this exhibit as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, can you tell us who made these markings on the photos, the circles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. These markings were done by Case Manager for Milosevic trial, the OTP -- the member of the OTP, Iain Reid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And who decided about the location of these circles? Was it technically made by the Case Manager or was he assisting another person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This exhibit has been prepared for Milosevic trial. It meant to be used for that trial but it wasn't. So -- and he was supporting on the investigative team with this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. This set of photographs on this page will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 6575 will be Exhibit P1027, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me just ask one other question before we break.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do the photographs that we've seen in P1027, do they conform to your independent observations of the video footage that we've seen in court today and that you've looked at in preparation for your testimony?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they do. And most probably I would do something similar and just not to repeat the work once more. That's what I found on the OTP system, and then I considered it as an important and very useful exhibit for this trial, that's why I picked it up and wanted to present this one. But I would be able to -- to do it the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think it's the break time, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Indeed, Mr. Vanderpuye, we have our second break now, and we will resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, I wanted to go through the last pair of videos that we have. The first one, we have an indicated date of December 2nd, 2nd December 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: For the record, it's 65 ter 5499.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you have familiarity with this video footage?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you tell us a little bit about it by way of background what it shows and the context in which it's shot.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a ceremony taking place at the stadium -- soccer field, actually, in Vlasenica on 2nd December 1995, when the Drina Corps -- Drina Corps Manoeuvre Brigade has been established.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can you tell us just generally who is featured in this -- in this video footage.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are several VRS Main Staff officers present, including General Ratko Mladic, Colonel Ljubisa Beara. Then the commander of the Drina Corps, General Radoslav Krstic. There is also Legenda, Jolovic Milan. And also the others -- the other members of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in terms of the chain of custody or the means by which the Office of the Prosecutor acquired this particular video footage, can you give us an idea of how that occurred?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This one was also obtained during the search of General Mladic's son apartment in Belgrade on 4th of December, 2008, and it was handed over to the OTP on -- in April 2009, along with other original stuff which was seized, and it was marked by the authorities of the Republic of Serbia as tape number 29.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And just for Your Honours' information, that was referred to -- I don't have the P number for it right now. 6578. This was the exhibit, as you recall, with the missing page in it, P1017, and it refers to item number 20 in that -- in that search inventory list. What I'd like to do now is play the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you tell us just in this frame right now that we've frozen continue at, who's depicted in it? I'm sorry, it's at 21 seconds in this frame.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the first individual with his back to the camera and with a black beret who is saluting to General Ratko Mladic is Legenda. Jolovic -- his name is Jolovic Milan. He was the commander of the Drina Wolves during the -- in July 1995, part of the Zvornik Brigade, but, at this time, he is becoming the commander of this newly established Manoeuvre Brigade of the Drina Corps. The individual who Legenda is saluting to is General Ratko Mladic. Behind Ratko Mladic is General Radoslav Krstic, at the time the commander of the Drina Corps. And we've seen just few seconds before, also there is additional individual behind General Krstic. We don't see him right now, but that one is Colonel Ljubisa Beara. He is the officer of the security department -- actually, the chief of the security department of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We can continue. We'll continue playing from here forward.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you tell us who is in the frame now that we've stopped at 34 seconds in this video?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we have these same VRS members. In addition, we have the man who is the last -- or the first from the left on this video, in glasses with grey hair, this is Colonel Ljubisa Beara.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And how do you recognise these individuals? What's your basis of knowledge to be able to identify them here?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
