utterances.text: They were identified several times by different individuals whose statement I've read. And also, in addition, for Legenda, for Jolovic, he -- General Mladic is referring to him during the speech he will make later on in this ceremony. For General Radoslav Krstic and Ljubisa Beara, they were both indictees, accused in this Tribunal. Ljubisa Beara for Popovic case, and General Krstic for its own case.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And with respect to your identification of Jolovic Milan, Legenda, so far we have only seen the back of his head. Are you able to make that identification from other footage in this clip?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. And I have to emphasis here that this is only an excerpt of a long video, and I reviewed the entire video. What we have here is just portion of it, and based on what we can see on the entire video, yes, I was able to recognise him, and I can say I confirm that this is the same person, that that's him.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I just wanted to point out to you that it was our intention, in terms of all these video-clips, to tender both the clip, that is, the excerpted part of the and the video as we received it in its entirety, so that if it is admitted, you can review in its full context. The reason we have it in clip form now is just for the sake of brevity, ironically. But we can continue from here forward.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would like to tender this video as well. I know that we have a standing ruling to have it marked for identification, so I -- I guess I'll modify my application in that respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I ask the witness about the source from where you or the OTP was able to obtain this video?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it is part of the collection of the material which was seized on 4 December 2004 during the search of Ratko Mladic's son apartment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. And, sorry, I repeated that -- that you had to repeat that. You said it earlier. Do you know if that was part of a public television service or something like that? Or is it only a video it was found in the apartment of General Mladic's son?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You can see from the video itself that there are at this ceremony three cameras present, and one of those was being public TV station, and the OTP has been, before that, already in possession of that video from the public station, and this video is part of the VRS camera. And it was even noted on the VHS tape itself that it is celebration in Vlasenica on 2nd of December, 20 -- 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This video will be marked for identification. I would like to add provisionally.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me just ask --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, please always wait.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: If we want to have marked it, we need the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you. 65 ter 5499 will be Exhibit P1028, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me just ask you, Mr. Janc, have you had an opportunity to view this other footage that you've referred to, of this same event?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have had the opportunity to review also the other version of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And does it conform to the version of the events that we've just seen now in court, or are there any differences in that footage?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are some difference, because it's different camera and certain events you can see from different angle. But all the rest is the same. And this version we have just seen is much more extensive one than what we have had before.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I'd like to ask you about the final video we have, and that's, for the record, 65 ter 5498. And that relates to an event on 13 January 1996. Are you familiar with this video footage?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar also with this footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you tell us briefly what the source of the footage was, or is, with respect to its acquisition by the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the same as for the previous one. It was seized during the search on 4 December 2008, and later on obtained or sent by the authorities of the Republic of Serbia to the OTP, and it was -- this video was actually marked as a video with sequence number 52.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's -- that's item number 52 in the P1017. This is the exhibit with the missing page that was fixed, for the record. And can you tell us briefly who's depicted in this video, what the context of it is.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's actually the celebration of the Orthodox new year from 13 January to 14 January 1996. It's taking place in Han Pijesak, and -- sorry, in Crna Rijeka, not in Han Pijesak, and it is a lot of general -- VRS Main Staff generals present celebrating this event, along with -- with -- with others here. I mean, General Mladic's wife is there also, and also the other generals. We can see them from the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Before we get started with that, can you tell us, was General Tolimir there?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he is not -- he was not there. And we cannot see him on a video either. And from a speech which was made by General Mladic, he refers to him, and he says that he is absent and he -- that is he in Vienna at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think we can start this one. We can play it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, are you able to identify or recognise anyone in this frame? We've stopped at 3 minutes, it appears, in this clip.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. First individual from the right-hand side, smoking a cigarette, he is General Milan Gvero. On his right-hand side, sitting next to it, is General Manojlo Milovanovic, he was Chief of the Staff of the Main Staff, VRS Main Staff. Then we have one woman which I cannot recognise. Then next to that woman we see on this video General Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Is there anybody else you are able to recognise or -- or is that it for now?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From this frame, I am -- I'm not sure, but I think that the person with the grey hair towards the end of this footage on the left-hand side, it's General Radivoje Miletic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And just so that the Trial Chamber is familiar with who that is, can you tell us who General Radivoje Miletic is.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was one of the accused in Popovic et al trial, and he was the member of the Main Staff, the chief of operations, and he has been, at the time, during Srebrenica events, replacing Chief of Staff, General Milivoje Milovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what's your basis of knowledge with respect to the identification of the individuals that you've made in this frame?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For General Milan Gvero and Radivoje Miletic, I can say that they were both accused in Popovic and all case. For General Manojlo Milovanovic, I met him personally here during the proofing session, so I know him, and I -- I can confirm that's him sitting there. And also from -- from the videos, especially for General Milan Gvero, I can say that there is many, many videos which I have reviewed during my -- my working here at the Tribunal where he was several times referred as General Gvero and then he is making speeches, so it's not -- it's for General Gvero, it is very easy to identify him.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And for the sake of the record, I'm not sure if that was recorded correctly in line 19 of page 65, you speak -- you are recorded as having mentioned General Milovanovic. Were you referring to him or to a different person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I'm referring to General Manojlo Milovanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. I think we can continue on from here.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd like to tender this video as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be marked for identification; and, again, at -- provisionally marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1029, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: During the course of the speech given by General Mladic, Mr. Janc, he made reference to someone by the name of Furtula, someone by the name of Trivic, and someone by the name of Kusic in relation to Zepa. Can you just tell the Trial Chamber who these individuals are as the investigations and your involvement in them have revealed?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rajko Kusic, he was the commander of Rogatica Brigade at the time, in July of 1995. Radomir Furtula, he was the commander of one of the Podrinje Brigade from Visegrad at the time. So I cannot remember the -- the number of the brigade, but that's him. And the third one was Mirko Trivic. He was the commander of the 2nd Romanija Corps -- 2nd Romanija Brigade, not corps, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And as the investigation -- well, let me ask you, does the investigation confirm what General Mladic was saying, concerning the involvement of these units in the Zepa campaign?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it -- it confirms. Because all of those units were involved in the Zepa operation. So it confirms, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that, Mr. Janc. That concludes my direct of you. I thank you very much for your participation and I thank you for your indulgence.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Your Honours, there was one matter that was left unattended and that was with respect to Mr. Janc's qualification of a certain document. It was a MUP document dated 1 July 1995, and I think, Mr. President, Your Honour asked for the source of that information and Mr. Janc responded that he'd need to check it. And I would like to have him do that so that we can provide that information to the Court, but we need your leave in order to have him do that. So I would ask for that. The document, more particularly, is P1025; it was marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We talked about that earlier, the order or report of Ljubisa Borovcanin; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We would appreciate to receive this additional information with the assistance of Mr. Janc. I would like to know, do you intend further examination-in-chief of Mr. Janc for another topic, or what is your position?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. We don't have anything in mind at the moment. It -- the circumstance may arise where we -- where we may have scheduling issues which we may be able to introduce further evidence through Mr. Janc or perhaps through another investigator. But, at the moment, we don't have anything specifically planned for him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Tolimir, your cross-examination which started before the summer recess was just interrupted, and I would like to ask you, are you prepared to continue with your cross-examination today in the last ten minutes of today's hearings, or would you like to do that at a later stage?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. If you want us to proceed, then I would like to deal with the topic at hand; whereas, the other matters would be addressed at a later stage as soon as the OTP calls the relevant witness. Or if you should so decide, we can continue at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, Mr. Tolimir, my question was the other way around. It is up to you. You should decide. Because after this lengthy examination-in-chief, perhaps you need more time for preparation of your cross-examination. But if you are prepared, we can use the last ten minutes and you should proceed. But it's up to you to decide.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I don't believe that we can even have a look at the relevant documents in e-court in the remaining ten minutes. I believe it would only be a waste of time. We still need to upload some of the relevant documents. We haven't had time to do that, and it would take too long to do it now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This was my expectation, and therefore, I think it's better not to continue with your cross-examination today. We should do that at a later stage and then you can prepare properly. Mr. Vanderpuye, what is your plan for next week?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think we have Mr. Clark coming on Tuesday. Then we have ...

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I understand that we have several hours that have been estimated for Mr. Clark. I think we have a cross-examination or Defence estimate of three or four hours for him.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Then we have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We don't need --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think we have a second witness after that who is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes. I just wanted to know in which way we will proceed on Tuesday, because we are not sitting on Monday and only three days next week.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We do have a witness lined up for Tuesday for sure and a following witness. I also wanted to mention, since the cross-examination of Mr. Janc will be put off but he obviously still works for the Office of the Prosecutor and we do need to have contact with him in relation to other matters concerning his responsibilities and also concerning the future investigation and the course of the case, we do need the Court's leave to have contact with him and so I'm asking for that as well. I don't know -- and I don't know, I don't believe that the Defence has any objection to that given the circumstances, but there it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think there's no problem, because we -- we are in the same situation after the first part of the examination of this witness. There's no concern. Otherwise, you wouldn't get a salary for your work if you are not able to work. Of course, but, on the other hand, you should restrict your contact with the witness to additional information related to the document we have mentioned earlier, P1025, MFI, and, otherwise, of course, Mr. Janc should work in the normal way. Are there any other matters to raise now? I don't think so. So that we have to adjourn now. We will resume on Tuesday next week in the morning at 9.00 in this courtroom. And for Monday, we wish you, Mr. Tolimir, all the best. Thank you very much. We adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 28th day of September, 2010, at 9.00 a.m. 25
